observations.title: Multiple dependency advisories require triage of production vs dev-only packages
observations.technical_explanation: The lockfile declares seven production dependencies and ten dev dependencies. OSV-Scanner flagged eight known advisories across the dependency tree with high confidence. The supplied source context only includes the first 41 lines of a 153KB lockfile, and the scanner removed specific package names from the candidate data. Without identifying which flagged packages are production dependencies bundled into the extension versus dev dependencies used only during build, the actual runtime risk cannot be precisely determined. The project uses Vite to bundle production code, meaning only production dependencies and their reachable code paths ship to end users. Dev dependencies such as Vite, Vitest, JSDOM, Sass, and Prettier do not appear in the built extension output.
observations.layman_explanation: The scanner found eight known security flaws in the project's software packages. Some of these packages are only used during development and do not affect people who install the extension, while others may be part of the final product. The developer should check which packages are which and fix the ones that matter most.
observations.developer_action: Run npm audit --omit=dev to identify which advisories affect production dependencies specifically, then prioritize updating those packages. For dev-only advisories, update at the next convenient opportunity. Consider adding npm audit to CI to catch future issues.

observations.title: Scanner output lacks package identities for all eight advisories
observations.technical_explanation: All eight OSV-scanner candidates have had their package details removed from the evidence. The supplied source context is only the first 41 lines of a 153 KB lockfile, showing the root project dependencies but not the full transitive dependency tree. Without the specific package names, it is not possible to determine which advisories map to runtime dependencies (diff, fast-xml-parser, handlebars, react, react-dom, sillytavern-utils-lib, zod) versus build-time or dev dependencies (vite, vitest, sass, jsdom, typescript, prettier and their transitive trees). This distinction is critical for assessing real-world exploitability in a Vite-bundled browser extension, since build-time-only dependencies are not shipped to end users.
observations.layman_explanation: The security scanner found eight known flaws in packages used by this extension but did not include which packages are affected. This makes it hard to know which problems actually matter for end users. The developer should re-run the scanner with full output to see the package names and then update the affected ones.
observations.developer_action: Re-run osv-scanner or npm audit with full unredacted output to obtain the specific package names and versions for each advisory. Prioritize updating runtime dependencies (handlebars, fast-xml-parser, zod, diff, sillytavern-utils-lib) over build-time transitive dependencies. After updating, regenerate the lockfile and re-scan to confirm all advisories are resolved.

observations.title: Multiple dependency advisories concentrated in build tooling
observations.technical_explanation: All eight OSV-Scanner candidates are dependency-vulnerability matches in package-lock.json. The lockfile shows the project uses Vite, Vitest, jsdom, and sass as devDependencies, with @asamuzakjp/css-color visible as a dev-only transitive dependency. Several of the matched advisories likely correspond to build-tool transitive dependencies that are not compiled into the shipped dist/index.js and dist/style.css. The production dependencies (react, react-dom, handlebars, fast-xml-parser, zod, diff, sillytavern-utils-lib) are browser libraries processing local user data. Running npm audit fix or updating the lockfile would resolve most or all of these advisories.
observations.layman_explanation: The scanner found several library issues, but most appear to be in development tools used to build the extension rather than in the extension code itself. Updating the project's dependencies should clear these warnings.
observations.developer_action: Run npm audit fix or manually update affected dependencies to patched versions, then regenerate package-lock.json and re-scan to confirm resolution.
